canonical_question: How does the 'matrix/ordered oxygen complex interface' structure influence dislocation motion compared to the grain boundaries?

question_variants.question: How does the 'matrix/ordered oxygen complex interface' structure influence dislocation motion compared to the grain boundaries?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text provides compositional profiles (enrichment/depletion) at the matrix/complex interface but does not describe the specific structural influence of this interface on dislocation motion compared to grain boundaries.

answers.answer: The text describes the compositional distribution (enrichment of O, Ti, Zr; depletion of Ta, Nb, Hf) at the matrix/ordered oxygen complex interface but does not compare this to grain boundaries or explain the specific dislocation motion mechanism.
answers.measurement_outcome: Proxigram showing enrichment of O, Ti, Zr and slight depletion of Ta, Nb, Hf.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison of interface vs grain boundary dislocation motion provided.
evidence_spans: It is also important to note that the peak temperature of damping in the current Snoek-type high-damping HEAs is approximately 100 K higher than that in traditional high-damping alloys ( [11] , [12] , [31] – [42] ).

Because of the high configuration entropy and severely distorted lattices of HEAs ( [50] ), atomic position switches of interstitials in these matrices are impeded by the high atomic-scale distortion fields ( [51] ).
This effect gives rise to the high activation temperatures and barrier energies for the interstitial reorientation steps and the resulting high-temperature damping capability.
